summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, ICD placement, diabetes, hypertension, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for acute dyspnea on exertion and leg weakness. Symptoms were likely due to mild volume overload from acute on chronic systolic heart failure, supported by elevated BNP, bilateral lung crackles, and radiographic evidence of mild pulmonary edema. He also had a productive cough suggestive of bronchitis. He received intravenous furosemide with resolution of symptoms and was able to ambulate without difficulty. Renal function was initially impaired with a creatinine of 1.7, improving to 1.6 during the stay. Lisinopril was held due to kidney concerns, with plans for outpatient reevaluation. Daytime somnolence was attributed to a high dose of imipramine, which was reduced at discharge. He was discharged home with instructions on weight monitoring, fluid and sodium restriction, and follow-up for lab work and psychiatric evaluation.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage I through stage IV, or unspecified
